observations.text: SP flew the TACAN final approach to the level required for this stage; however, the descent from the FAF was initiated only after the IP directed it, and the stepdown restrictions published in the Instrument Approach Manual were respected only after the IP called each fix. Level-off was reached with the aircraft 200 ft above MDA and the final approach course displaced 10 degrees before the IP corrected the heading. Marginal performance for the Training Section - independent management of the final approach segment is expected to improve on the following sorties.

SP, working from the standardized VOR/DME final approach procedure of AFMAN 11-202 VOL3, flew the segment from the FAF to the MAP without the IP having to direct or execute any part of it. Descent to the published stepdown altitudes was initiated after two verbal prompts from the IP, and the final approach course was held to 8 degrees of the published radial. Level-off occurred 200 ft above MDA and the computed final approach airspeed reached 15 knots fast, with the deviations recognized and corrected, although with delay. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP briefed and flew the TACAN approach in accordance with the published procedure, complying with ATC instructions and with the routing and altitude restrictions of the Instrument Approach Manual without prompting. Minor errors in the descent rate after the FAF left the aircraft 150 ft above MDA at the point where level-off was planned, and the final approach course opened to 7 degrees, both recognized and corrected by the SP in a timely manner. No IP intervention was required at any point of the final segment. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the VOR/DME final approach accurately and quickly, starting the descent at the FAF and meeting every stepdown altitude published in the Instrument Approach Manual. The final approach course was held within 3 degrees of the published radial, the computed final approach airspeed within 5 knots, and MDA was captured 50 ft high with no descent below it. ATC instructions were complied with without prompting and no IP intervention was required. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP knew and executed the TACAN final approach flawlessly, transitioning to the final approach course and to the computed final approach airspeed without hesitation. The raw radial and DME picture was cross-checked continuously against the descent profile, holding the course within 1 degree, the airspeed within 3 knots and MDA within 20 ft with no descent below it. Accuracy and speed at the MAP were above the levels desired for this stage of training. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a non-standardized final approach flow that left the descent point undefined, did not initiate the descent at the FAF and did not comply with the stepdown altitudes published in the Instrument Approach Manual. The aircraft passed the stepdown fix 350 ft high and then descended through MDA, with the result that the IP took control and executed the level-off. Review of the VOR/TACAN approach procedure in the Flight Manual is required before the next instrument sortie.

SP, due to inadequate workload management during the approach phase, left the approach checklist unfinished and did not set the final approach course on the HSI before the FAF. The aircraft crossed the FAF 20 knots fast and diverged 15 degrees from the published radial, with the result that the IP had to direct the reintercept and execute part of the descent to MDA. The final approach segment could not be completed without assistance.

SP flew the VOR/TACAN final approach to the standard required for this stage, completing the segment after the IP's verbal prompts at the FAF and at each stepdown fix. Deviations were recognized and corrected with delay, the final approach course reaching 8 degrees from the published radial and the computed final approach airspeed 15 knots fast before the corrections took effect. Marginal performance for the Training Section - earlier recognition of the course and airspeed trends is expected to improve on the following sorties.

SP flew the TACAN approach from the FAF to the MAP without IP prompting, complying with ATC instructions and with the routing and altitude restrictions published in the Instrument Approach Manual. Minor errors in the initial descent rate produced a level-off 150 ft above MDA and a course deviation of 6 degrees, both identified by the SP and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the VOR/DME final approach according to standardized procedures, setting the final approach course and the computed final approach airspeed before the FAF and descending on profile to each published stepdown altitude. The course was held within 4 degrees, the airspeed within 8 knots fast, and MDA was maintained with a maximum deviation of 80 ft above and no descent below. Accuracy and speed were demonstrated without prompting or IP intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP knew and executed the VOR/TACAN final approach flawlessly, complying with every ATC instruction and every published routing and altitude restriction without prompting. The final approach course was held within 2 degrees of the published radial, the computed final approach airspeed within 3 knots, and MDA was captured within 30 ft with the MAP identified on time. Deviations were negligible throughout the segment and accuracy exceeded the levels desired for this stage of training. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an incorrect setting of the final approach course on the HSI, tracked a radial displaced from the one published in the Instrument Approach Manual and did not identify the FAF at the correct DME. The aircraft descended outside the published final approach segment and reached 250 ft below the stepdown altitude, with the result that the IP directed the reintercept and executed the go-around. The approach could not be completed without assistance.

SP, due to inadequate monitoring of airspeed during the approach, allowed the computed final approach airspeed to decay 20 knots below the value briefed for the configuration while the descent to MDA continued. The airspeed trend was not recognized on the instrument cross-check, with the result that the IP had to intervene on the power lever and direct the recovery to the profile. Consistent cross-check of airspeed against the descent profile is required before the next instrument sortie.

SP, due to a delayed transition from the arc to the final approach course, began the turn late and rolled out beyond the published radial without an immediate correction. The course deviation reached 8 degrees and the aircraft crossed the FAF 200 ft above the published altitude, corrected only after the IP's verbal prompts. Deviations were recognized and corrected with delay, without the IP having to take control.

SP, due to distraction by radio traffic while established on final, interrupted the instrument cross-check between the FAF and MDA and did not monitor the descent rate against the published profile. The computed final approach airspeed reached 15 knots fast and the aircraft levelled off 200 ft above MDA, corrected only after the IP called the deviations. Recognition and correction were achieved with delay and without IP intervention on the controls.

SP flew the TACAN final approach within the desired standards, complying with ATC instructions and with the published routing and altitude restrictions, and correcting the deviations without the IP's intervention. However, the accuracy remained at the edge of the standard, with the final approach course twice reaching 7 degrees from the published radial and the computed final approach airspeed 12 knots fast before the corrections took effect. Marginal performance for the Training Section - a tighter cross-check between the FAF and MDA is expected to improve.

SP executed the VOR/DME final approach accurately and quickly, identifying the FAF at the correct DME and descending to each published stepdown altitude on profile. The final approach course was held within 4 degrees, the computed final approach airspeed within 7 knots fast, and MDA was captured 60 ft high with no descent below it. No prompting or IP intervention was required and the MAP was identified on time. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP knew and executed the VOR/TACAN final approach flawlessly, in an impeccable and standardized manner, from the initial approach fix to the MAP. The raw radial and DME information was cross-checked continuously against the descent profile, holding the final approach course within 1 degree, the computed final approach airspeed within 3 knots and MDA within 20 ft with no descent below. ATC instructions and every published restriction were complied with without prompting, and the deviations remained negligible throughout. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to failure to identify the correct FAF and to start the timing required for the approach without DME, descended before the published descent point and did not comply with the altitude restrictions of the Instrument Approach Manual. The aircraft was 300 ft below the stepdown altitude and 12 degrees off the published radial, with the result that the IP took control and executed the climb back to the segment altitude. The approach could not be completed without assistance.

SP, due to over-reliance on the GPS overlay without an independent check of the raw TACAN parameters, did not verify the final approach course and the DME distances against the Instrument Approach Manual. The aircraft was flown down a track displaced 14 degrees from the published radial and descended below MDA before the MAP, with the result that the IP took control and executed the missed approach. The raw navigation picture must be cross-checked against the published procedure on every approach.

SP, due to a late configuration change that was not completed before the FAF, could not stabilize the computed final approach airspeed on the descent to MDA. The airspeed reached 15 knots fast and 10 knots slow within the same segment and the final approach course opened to 8 degrees, corrected only after the IP's verbal prompts at each deviation. The approach was completed without the IP taking control, but recognition and correction were delayed throughout.

SP, due to lack of knowledge of the published stepdown structure for the approach flown, did not plan the descent between the FAF and MDA and levelled off at each altitude only when the IP called the fix. MDA was reached 200 ft high with the aircraft 8 degrees off the published radial at the MAP, both corrected after verbal prompting. Study of the VOR/TACAN plates and of the descent gradients required is expected before the next instrument sortie.

SP, due to a descent rate selected without reference to the groundspeed after the FAF, arrived at MDA later than the profile required and did not level off at the planned point. The final approach course opened to 6 degrees and the aircraft was 150 ft above MDA approaching the MAP, both recognized by the SP and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention. Adjustment of the descent rate to the groundspeed is expected on the following approaches.

SP, due to complacency on an approach flown repeatedly on previous sorties, relaxed the instrument cross-check between the FAF and MDA and monitored the raw course indication only intermittently. The final approach course reached 7 degrees from the published radial and the computed final approach airspeed 12 knots fast, both identified by the SP and corrected without the IP's intervention. An active cross-check is expected on every approach regardless of familiarity.

SP executed the VOR/TACAN final approach according to standardized procedures, complying with ATC instructions and with every published routing and altitude restriction without IP intervention. However, the accuracy was at the edge of the desired standard, with the final approach course twice reaching 5 degrees from the published radial and MDA captured 100 ft high before the correction took effect. Marginal performance for the Training Section - a more immediate correction of the course and altitude trends is expected to improve.

SP knew and executed the TACAN final approach flawlessly, without the IP's intervention, in an impeccable and standardized manner from the FAF to the MAP. The raw radial and DME picture was cross-checked continuously against the descent profile, with the final approach course held within 1 degree, the computed final approach airspeed within 2 knots and MDA maintained within 20 ft and never violated. ATC instructions and the published restrictions of the Instrument Approach Manual were complied with without prompting, and accuracy and speed were above the levels desired for this stage of training. Above end of block MIF achieved.
